title: Example: retry queue for webhook delivery
verdict: Webhook delivery moves from fire-and-forget to an at-least-once outbox worker.

sections.heading: What changed
sections.md: Webhooks now **enqueue** into an `outbox` table instead of firing inline during the request. A worker claims rows with a lease and delivers them, retrying on failure.

sections.heading: New delivery path
sections.mermaid:
flowchart LR
  API[API handler] --> OB[(outbox table)]
  OB --> W[worker]
  W --> EP[endpoint]
  W -->|failure| OB

sections.title: At-least-once over exactly-once
sections.md: Receivers must **dedup by event id**. Exactly-once would require distributed transactions between our DB and every receiver.
Example annotation: in a real guide this points at the load-bearing hunk and explains what makes it safe.

sections.heading: Send path
sections.before_md: `send_webhook()` called inline; a slow endpoint stalls the request thread.
sections.after_md: Request writes one row; the worker owns delivery, retries, and backoff.

sections.md: Cap retries at 24h and dead-letter, or retry forever?
